params.body:
Vera's worker runs on Vera's own machine since today: its key `#agent-vera` was made there and never left, the machine opens its own IAP tunnel to the sealed machine on its own service account, and it holds its own client token. The gateway judges for `#agent-vera` from there.

The skill still assumed one place to stand, the operator's laptop, and relayed every submission over ssh to the Elixir box. That box holds the secrets of the whole fleet, so a product machine that could reach it that way would be able to read far more than its own work.

- The transport is chosen by a fact about the machine, not a flag: a client token beside the seed means this machine reaches the gateway itself (`fetch` to the tunnel on 127.0.0.1:8471), and without one the submission goes over ssh to the box as before.
- A flag would have to be remembered by whoever starts the worker; the file is there or it is not.
- `transport()` is exported and tested both ways.

Nothing changes for the laptop. What changes is that a second machine can act without the first.
params.title: Vera's eigen machine spreekt de gateway zelf
